title: Solo OLM Guide COX OSRS
summary: Gnomonkey teaches the solo Great Olm fight in a regular Chambers of Xeric, covering the 12:0 and 8:1 Tumeken's Shadow running methods and the 4:1 lance (Scythe) method. He explains how to get into cycle, null flame walls, deal with acid and crystals, and what to do when something goes wrong.

outline.text: 12:0 shadow running tiles and cycle (hits one to five)
8:1 shadow running: tanking a hit in the middle
Why start with the Shadow and the opening hand order
Using thralls and getting into cycle
4:1 lance method: tank two hits on the thumb
The three things that can happen on the thumb
Fixing the tick with a Scythe swing; starting the third phase in 4:1
Head running and flame wall nulling
Binding the attack style tab and spec bar; solo advice

claims.text: In the 12:0 Shadow running method Gnomonkey uses marked tiles numbered by the hit of the cycle: hit from one then run to the side and return, hit from two to be dragged and come back, hit from three, a long range hit from four, and hit from five, then repeat one to five until the hand is dead, usually about two cycles.
In the 8:1 Shadow running method you actually tank a hit: a long-range hit from one, run and come back, drag on the hit, then tank a hit in the middle on two, and get dragged on three, repeating.
Gnomonkey says 8:1 is a lot harder than 12:0 because you actually tank a hit.

In 8:1 you tank the hit in the middle because when the head is on flame phase and does a flame wall, standing on that tile nulls it and he just makes a motion with nothing happening; you can equip ranged armour quickly to block some damage.

Gnomonkey says to start with the Shadow because the melee hand cripples if you attack it with melee before the mage hand is dead; the main idea is to hammer the melee hand, switch to mage and start running.

Gnomonkey says it is really important to use a thrall while learning, because the thrall keeps the hand turning all the way; if you splash or the thrall stops attacking, the hand turns mid-way, which makes it hard to learn.
To get into cycle, wait until Olm is about to turn and click from tile one; Gnomonkey says to hit a tick after he turns.
In the 4:1 lance method you go to the thumb, tank two hits, and then do the same thing every cycle, making sure you are hitting on the right tick.

On the thumb with 4:1 there are three outcomes: Olm uses a special attack (lightning, crystals, teleports) then another attack then nothing, so you wait an attack and run when he does nothing; he does two attacks in a row so you run immediately and do a three-to-one; or he stares at you and does nothing, in which case you are already in cycle.
If you attack on the same tick Olm turns (the wrong tick) and have a Scythe, you can swing the Scythe to fix it, and it even gives a bit more DPS for that swing.
For the crystal phase, Gnomonkey says it is super easy: do an L walk and just keep moving every tick, tanking a hit, then he does nothing and you are in cycle.

Gnomonkey says you can start the third phase with the melee hand because it does not clench, and with a hammer you can hammer, wait for him to turn and be in 4:1 every time; with two hammers it is tick perfect.
For acid, Gnomonkey says to just start attacking and do an L walk: step across, hit, come around, hit, hit, and repeat.
Gnomonkey says to remove boots at Olm if you can because it is a big difference: minus 12 mage accuracy.
For head running, move every time Olm turns so you line up with the cycle, and you tank a hit every four turns in the middle, which nulls flame walls.
Gnomonkey says you can null flame walls in 4:1 by standing on a specific tile when you tank the attack; on either side you tank the attack and then come in and it also nulls the flame wall.
Gnomonkey says if you ever lose a tick you should go back to one and start the cycle again; always fix the cycle.
Gnomonkey says if you are close and pulled up at the end it reduces the Twisted bow travel time so it kills him slightly faster, and he has never done a solo Olm without a Twisted bow.

Gnomonkey says dealing with acid and dealing with flame walls are the two things to know and that Shadow running and 4:1 are not hard, you just have to know what to do and not get pulled out of cycle by weird things.
Gnomonkey says you should probably do some team runs before solo Chambers of Xeric because solo is pretty hard.
Gnomonkey says a lot of people are scared of four-to-one and he was too for hundreds of kills because nobody explained it well and there were no good videos.
The video description says the solo Olm guide was mocked up on stream in a regular Chambers of Xeric, and that 12:0 and 8:1 Shadow running and 4:1 lance method are not tough to learn.
Gnomonkey says you need the long range attack style bound to run Shadow at solo Chambers of Xeric, and he binds a tab for the attack style, which he also finds useful in Chambers and Inferno.
Gnomonkey says the spec bar is really, really good because it lets you spec out so fast but takes a lot of practice, and he only started using it a couple of months before this stream.
Gnomonkey says his Shadow running method is the same as others on YouTube but he remembers it by labeled tiles and the hits of the cycle.
Gnomonkey says he is 6'2.
